annotations.title: Check a page is ready to be cited

description:
Check whether one page has what AI answers look for before they cite
it, for the question it should answer, and say exactly what to change,
before or after a page is edited. It reads the HTML a crawler gets, so
it also catches content that only appears with JavaScript.

Checks: the <title> asks the question and fits (60 characters); one
<h1> matching it; the first paragraph after the heading is the answer
itself (12 to 45 words, a sentence, with a number or date); a visible
"Updated" date that matches the JSON-LD dateModified and is under 90
days old; at least 300 words without JavaScript; valid structured data,
and FAQ markup only for questions shown on the page; canonical and
noindex; robots.txt letting OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot,
Claude-SearchBot and Googlebot reach the page.

Costs 0 quota units: it fetches the page and its robots.txt itself and
never calls the data provider. Read-only, safe to retry. Passing makes
a page easier to cite, it does not cause a citation: whether the
question is one your site can own matters more, which only
analyze_citation_coverage measures.

Returns: {"url" (after redirects), "question", "passed", "failed",
"fixes" (what to change, one line per failed check, in page order),
"checks" (each {"rule", "ok", "observed", "fix"}), "basis" (one
sentence on where the checks come from)}, or {"url", "error"} when the
page cannot be fetched (not public, not HTML, an HTTP error).

Args:
    url: full address of the page, e.g. "https://example.com/pricing".
    question: what the page should answer, in the words people search
        with, e.g. "how much does example cost".
name: check_page_readiness
title: Check a page is ready to be cited
